newsitem.title: UK: Weak Wall St depresses European bourses.
newsitem.headline: Weak Wall St depresses European bourses.

text.p: Leading European stock markets closed at around their lowest levels of a lacklustre day on Tuesday after profit-taking pushed down Wall Street by more than half-a-percent.
Bourses had earlier been mixed or lower in thin trade, nervously expecting Wall Street to cash in on gains after its record closing high on Monday.
Market sentiment was further weighed down by continuing worries about interest rate hikes.
On the currency markets, the dollar recovered somewhat from earlier losses against the mark and yen and traders said its underlying tone remained firm.
In London, Europe's busiest stock exchange, shares ended weaker, dragged downwards by falling bonds, a weaker Dow and a call for higher interest rates from the Bank of England's deputy governor.
The FTSE 100 index closed 27.7 points down at 4,078.8, just above the day's low, with decliners in a seven-to-two majority. The Dow was off 50 points shortly after London closed.

"We seem to be ignoring the Dow on the upside but following it on the downside," said Philip Isherwood, strategist at Kleinwort Benson. "Bonds weakened over lunchtime and the Dow has come back a long way from yesterday's high."

In Frankfurt, German shares recovered morning losses to end afternoon bourse trade slightly up but they slid in electronic trading after the New York opening. The IBIS DAX index of off floor trade ended down nearly half-a-percent.
German stocks had been unmoved by news of industrial orders rising an expected 0.5 percent in November compared to October.

It was a similar story in Paris where French shares, hampered by falling bond prices, closed easier in line with Wall Street but remained above the key 2,300 level, some 60 points shy of the CAC-40 index historic high set in February, 1994.

Both equity and currency traders said markets were nervous ahead of key U.S. statistics due out later in the week -- Thursday's producer price index and Friday's non-farm payrolls -- which will give clues to future movements of U.S. interest rates.

On the currency markets the dollar fell to its session lows in the afternoon as U.S. stock and bond markets opened weaker but recovered some lost ground in late trade. A smaller-than -expected drop in U.S. November factory goods orders had little impact.
"We've seen some important lows at 1.5540 marks and 115 yen today and bounced off them. I think the bulk of the selling is out of the way now," said Banque Paribas technical analyst Andrew Chevariat.
The U.S. currency had slipped from 45-month highs of 117 yen overnight after Japanese officials warned against excessive yen weakness.

Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said an excessively weak or strong yen was unfavourable for Japan's economy and his views were echoed by trade Minister Shinji Sato, who said an excessively weak yen was troublesome for the economy.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5635 marks and 115.35 yen compared with 1.5665 and 115.60 in late European trade on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING INDICES
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 27.7 points lower at 4,078.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 4.98 at 2,301.69.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 4.81 at 2,886.13. The IBIS DAX ended down 13.86 points at 2876.34.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed in Europe at $359.35, up from London's Monday close of $357.95. Silver finished slightly higher at $4.72.
